issues.author: Soumya Sinha
issues.subject: Validation Missing for Non-Onboarded Switched Vendor in Web and Mobile Applications
issues.description:
1. When an enquiry is created with multiple vendors and a trip is created using a vendor that already exists in the ERP, switching the trip to another vendor who is not yet onboarded allows the user to click Send for Approval and proceed with the approval process.

This is incorrect behavior and should be consistent across both the Web and Mobile applications.

Current Behavior:

Create an enquiry with two vendors.
Create a trip using a vendor that already exists in the ERP.
Switch the trip to another vendor who is not onboarded.
Click Send for Approval.
The system allows the approval process to continue without validating the vendor onboarding status.
Validation is shown only when the user clicks the Onboard Vendor button.
The same issue is present in the Mobile application, where further approval is allowed even after switching to a non-onboarded vendor.

Expected Behavior:

If the selected vendor is not onboarded, the system should not allow the user to proceed with Send for Approval in either the Web or Mobile application.
A validation message such as "Selected vendor is not onboarded. Please complete vendor onboarding before sending for approval." should be displayed.
The user should be able to continue with the approval process only after the vendor onboarding is successfully completed.
The validation should be triggered automatically when Send for Approval is clicked and should not depend on the user clicking the Onboard Vendor button.

issues.author: Soumya Sinha
issues.subject: Incorrect Accommodation Validation Triggered for Valid Travel Date
issues.description:
When submitting an accommodation expense, the system throws an incorrect validation error even though the accommodation dates match the travel itinerary.

Steps to Reproduce:

Create a Travel Claim with the following itinerary:
23/07/2026: Trivandrum → Bangalore
24/07/2026: Bangalore → Chennai
25/07/2026: Chennai → Trivandrum
Add an Accommodation expense in Bangalore with:
Check-in: 23/07/2026
Check-out: 24/07/2026
Submit the expense.

Actual Result:
The system displays the following validation error:

"On 2026-07-24 your pan-India travel places you in Chennai (TN), so accommodation in BANGALORE (KA) is not allowed."

Expected Result:
The accommodation should be accepted because the employee stayed in Bangalore from 23/07/2026 to 24/07/2026, and travelling to Chennai on 24/07/2026 does not invalidate the accommodation for the previous night's stay. The validation should correctly consider the accommodation period and travel schedule before raising an error.

issues.author: Amal Prasad
issues.subject: 4. Exposure Ratio Control
issues.description:
New "Exposure Ratio Required" checkbox at onboarding; 3-month grace period from first trip before activation.
Formula: Exposure Ratio = (Ledger Balance + Unbilled Trips − Collections) ÷ Avg. past 3 months invoiced amount, recalculated monthly.
Configurable thresholds: Warning at 2.5 (alert email + trip banner), Restriction at ≥3.0 (trip creation blocked + notifications).
CR flow for temporary additional credit limit (value + validity days) to lift restriction, auto-reverting on expiry; approval via Manager → Finance Manager.

Acceptance Criteria: All fields/flows reflected correctly in Customer Master, alerts/notifications trigger as specified, CR approvals logged in timeline & history tab, and no disruption to existing approval workflows.

CR-based flows for: Agreement Last Date extension (max +30 days), Payment Terms change, Finance Estimated Margin % change, and Credit Limit change — all via User → Manager → Finance Manager approval, logged in timeline/history.

Remove the Segment field (mandatory UH/FTL choice) from the Vendor Lead onboarding form.
Onboard vendors directly into the fleet via a single, unified flow with no category selector.
Once onboarded, the vendor must be immediately available for selection under both FTL and UH contexts wherever vendor selection occurs downstream (e.g. trip creation, vendor assignment) — all such dropdowns/lookups must query the same vendor master.


2. Auto-duplicate vendor across companies

On save/approval of onboarding under either company, automatically create a corresponding vendor record under the other company — no manual re-onboarding required.
Each company-level record gets its own unique vendor ID per that company's numbering series, while core details (name, contact, PAN, GSTIN, bank details, etc.) carry over to both.
Vendor selection screens in both companies must reflect the duplicated record immediately.

issues.author: Sachin Jaipal
issues.subject: Customer Advance amount - FTL
issues.description:
NOTE: *Additional requirement (Not in BRD) --> Once customer advance is entered, don't allow customer name change in new stage. And using CR if the customer is change, then the customer advance entry made is cancelled, then an intimation is given during the same time, to enter new advance amount. For that if Invoice is posted, it should be cancelled.* 

# Work Order — Customer Financial Details

Add a new "Customer Advance" amount field alongside Customer Price / Add-charge / Deduction / Total Customer Price.
Editable by Finance roles until an invoice is posted against the WO; read-only thereafter.


# Invoice Form — Advance Amount row

Auto-populate the existing (currently static) "Advance Amount" row from the WO's Customer Advance value.
Read-only on the invoice screen; any correction must be made at the WO before invoice generation.
Used in the invoice's payable-amount calculation.


# Invoice List View — "Advance Amt" column

Populate this column per invoice at creation/posting, reflecting only the amount actually applied to that specific invoice (relevant for partial invoicing scenarios).


# Business Rules — Advance Netting on Partial Invoicing

Rule 1: If a partial invoice amount is less than the Customer Advance, the advance is excluded from that invoice; it's invoiced/payable in full.
Rule 2: After any partial invoice, the remaining (un-invoiced) WO balance must stay ≥ the Customer Advance. If not, block posting and prompt the user to reduce the partial amount or raise the final invoice instead.
Rule 3: These rules ensure the advance is netted only against an invoice (partial or final) large enough to absorb it, not split across multiple small partials.


# Payable Calculation:

Amount Due = Customer Total Amount − Customer Advance Amount (applied at the invoice where the advance is netted).

issues.author: Sachin Jaipal
issues.subject: Fleet Customer - Exposure ratio, finance margin, credilt limit type, Agreement last date.
issues.description:
This requirement covers four interrelated enhancements to the ERP–Fleet finance module, strengthening customer credit governance and risk monitoring without impacting the existing approval hierarchy.
1. Finance Estimated Margin %

New Finance-controlled benchmark field on Lead/Contract screen & Customer Master.
Alert banner on trips where actual margin falls below this benchmark; such trips route through Middle & Top level manager approval and appear on a dedicated FTL screen.

2. Credit Limit Type (Month-wise / Overall)

Extend existing Credit Limit field to support Month-wise (resets monthly) and Overall (standing limit) — both configurable per customer.
Exposure/credit tracking logic to evaluate utilisation based on selected type.

3. Agreement Last Date & Change Request

New field to set agreement submission deadline (max 60 days from customer's first trip); auto-restriction if not met, with prior (10-day) and post-restriction notifications to Ops Manager, Sales Person & Ops Executive.
CR-based flows for: Agreement Last Date extension (max +30 days), Payment Terms change, Finance Estimated Margin % change, and Credit Limit change — all via User → Manager → Finance Manager approval, logged in timeline/history.

4. Exposure Ratio Control

New "Exposure Ratio Required" checkbox at onboarding; 3-month grace period from first trip before activation.
Formula: Exposure Ratio = (Ledger Balance + Unbilled Trips − Collections) ÷ Avg. past 3 months invoiced amount, recalculated monthly.
Configurable thresholds: Warning at 2.5 (alert email + trip banner), Restriction at ≥3.0 (trip creation blocked + notifications).
CR flow for temporary additional credit limit (value + validity days) to lift restriction, auto-reverting on expiry; approval via Manager → Finance Manager.

Acceptance Criteria: All fields/flows reflected correctly in Customer Master, alerts/notifications trigger as specified, CR approvals logged in timeline & history tab, and no disruption to existing approval workflows.

KINDLY REFER THE BRD & ASK IF ANY CLARIFICATION REQUIRED

issues.author: Soumya Sinha
issues.subject: One-Day Prior E-way Bill Expiry Notification is Not Sent When Trip Remains In Transit
issues.description:
Description

As per the requirement, the system should send an E-way Bill expiry email notification one day before the E-way Bill expiry date and again on the E-way Bill expiry date, provided the trip is in the In Transit state.

For a verified E-way Bill with an expiry date of 03/07/2026, the expected behavior is:

If the Trip Date is 01/07/2026 and the trip remains in the In Transit state on 02/07/2026, an email notification should be sent on 02/07/2026 (one day before the expiry date).
If the Trip Date is 02/07/2026 and the trip is in the In Transit state, an email notification should also be sent on 02/07/2026, as it is one day before the E-way Bill expiry date.
If the trip remains in the In Transit state on 03/07/2026 (the E-way Bill expiry date), the user should receive email notifications on both 02/07/2026 (one day before expiry) and 03/07/2026 (on the expiry date).
Current Behavior

All E-way Bill expiry email notifications are generated only on 03/07/2026. No email notification is received on 02/07/2026, even though the trip is in the In Transit state one day before the E-way Bill expiry date.

Actual Result

The system generates E-way Bill expiry email notifications only on the E-way Bill expiry date (03/07/2026).

issues.author: Sachin Jaipal
issues.subject: Driver Payout batch - enhancement
issues.description:
Enhancement is required in the Driver Batch Payout workflow to automate COD refresh, deduction recomputation, and payout recalculation activities within the ERP payout process.
Once the Ops User sends the payout batch for verification, the system shall automatically trigger payout recomputation using the latest payout data available in the system. The automation shall refresh COD collections, deductions, incentives, penalties, and payable amounts.
After Finance Approval, the system shall automatically perform deduction computation again to ensure the latest deduction values are applied before payment processing.

issues.author: Sachin Jaipal
issues.subject: Vendor Payout Batch process
issues.description:
Enhancement is required in the Vendor Batch Payout workflow to introduce automated payout recalculation and deduction computation during the verification and finance approval stages.
Once the Ops User sends the batch for verification, the system shall automatically perform payout recalculation, including COD adjustments, deductions, recomputation, and related payout validations before Finance Verification.
After Finance Verification, the system shall again trigger an automated deduction computation process to ensure all latest deductions and payout adjustments are accurately applied before final payout approval.
A mail has to be sent to vendor to where the vendor can upload the Invoice & it will be attached to the respective payout batch.

issues.subject: Mobile App Version Update
issues.description:
Mobile Application Versioning & Release Management Guidelines

The current mobile application version is 1.0.2.
Going forward, all functionality deployments, enhancements, and bug fixes must be referenced against the corresponding application version for proper tracking and release management.

Any critical bug fix release must be configured as a forced update to ensure all users migrate to the latest stable version immediately, rather than relying on manual updates which users may overlook.
The next major mobile application release must be updated to Version 2.0.
Subsequent minor enhancements, patches, or small feature additions should follow incremental versioning, for example:
2.0.1
2.0.2
2.1
Any future major release involving significant functionality, architecture, or UI/UX changes should increment the major version accordingly, such as:
Version 3.0
Version 4.0
For every non-critical release, the latest application update link from the respective app store (Google Play Store / Apple App Store) must be shared along with the release notes so users can update the application at their convenience.

issues.author: Sachin Jaipal
issues.subject: External Surcharge & Tip - DDT, Sale Order, Payout
issues.description:
An additional field "External Surcharge" & "Tip" & "Rider Surcharge share" & "QWQER Surge share" is required in the Sale order & Daily drier transactions. The value for this field will be passed from the DMS. The value in this field is required to be considered in Driver Payout calculations. (Dependent on DMS side dev). The changes to be made in DE receivables report & Sales order/Invoice report, need to mention these columns also in the report to show the calculation.

Sale Order will show: 
* Total Surge Received - The total surge amount received from the customer.
* QWQER Surge Share - A split-up can be configured in DMS for the Total surge. So if any, then surge amount received for QWQER. 
* Rider Surge Share - A split-up can be configured in DMS for the Total surge. So if any, then surge amount received for Rider. 
* Tip Amount - The tip amount received for the rider.
Eg: Total Surge - Rs 10/- 
    Spit of 50/50, Then QWQER Surge - Rs 5/-, Rider Surge - Rs 5/-. 
This is done purely for reporting and reconciliation 

DDT and payout will also clearly show:  
* Surge earnings (Rider Surge Share)  
* Tip 

Reports : DE receivables report, need to show the Rider Surge Share & Tip Amount
          Sales order/Invoice report, need to show the Total Surge Received, QWQER Surge Share, Rider Surge Share, Tip Amount.

issues.author: Sachin Jaipal
issues.subject: Flow change in Approval – with & without Advance
issues.description:
*If the user creates claim asking for advance:*
 New claim with Advance --> Sent to Reporting manager for Approval --> sent to finance user for advance payment approval --> Expense submitted by user --> claim sent to finance user for approval --> If any line item exceeds limit or require special approval, then sent for special approval --> Once approved,Claim again reaches to finance user, Once approved --> Claim completed.

*If the user creates claim without advance: * 
New claim created --> Sent to Reporting manager for Approval --> Expense submitted by user --> claim sent to finance user for approval --> If any line item exceeds limit or require special approval, then sent for special approval --> Once approved,Claim again reaches to finance user, Once approved --> Claim completed.

NOTE: So the major difference is one layer of finance approval is removed if advance payment is not req. (Refer page 4 of doc)

issues.author: Mohammed Sadique
issues.subject: Enquiry & Vendor Quote Model Enhancement(field addition and view)
issues.description:
1) Enquiry Creation Functionality
Sales team creates enquiry with following fields:
• Customer Name (Existing customer selection) – Customer name can be selected here.
• Enquiry Nature (Contractual / Live Bidding / Spot Deployment) – Enquiry nature can
be selected from the option.
• Assigned User (Sales team member) – Sales user name auto populates.
• Region – Customer region will be auto populated.
• Enquiry Date & Time (Auto captured) – The date & time of enquiry creation will be
captured.
2) Deployment Details Functionality
Sales team enters Trip deployment details:
• Pickup City – The city where pickup is required can be selected from the list.
• Pickup Address – The address will be auto-populated with pickup city name, it can be
changed & user can enter required address.
• Destination City - The city where drop is required can be selected from the list.
• Destination Address - The address will be auto-populated with Destination city name,
it can be changed & user can enter required address.
• Deployment Basis (Tonnage / Truck Tyre / Fixed Truck) – This can be selected from
the given options.
• Vehicle Type – The required type can be selected from the list provided.
• Tonnage – User can enter the tonnage value of the load.
• Number of Vehicles – The no of vehicles can be entered here.
• Load Type – The description about the type of the load can be entered here by the user.
• Vehicle Required Date & Time – The required time & date of the vehicle can be
mentioned here by the user.
• Comments – If any additional info to be provided can be entered here as comments.
Deployment details saved, sent & is visible to Supply team.
3) Quote Submission Functionality
Supply team submits vendor quotes with following details:
• Vendor Name – The name of the Vendor can be selected from existing list or enter name
here.
• Vendor Type (Truck Owner / Broker) – The type can be selected from the option.
• Rate – The rate negotiated with the vendor can be entered here.
• Supply person Name (Auto populated) – The supply person name will auto populate
here.
• Edit rate – Supply person should be able to edit the submitted quote price if it’s in
pending state, i.e if not accepted, rejected or sent back for revision. And the changed
quote shouldn’t be greater than the earlier entered rate.
• Comments – Any additional info can be entered in comments before sending to sales
team.

issues.author: Sachin Jaipal
issues.subject: ERP - Pickup Distance Incentive Configuration in Rider Earnings
issues.description:
Currently, the Distance Incentive (Pickup → Drop) is configured in ERP and fetched for:
Estimated earnings display in DE app (per order)
Today’s earnings calculation
Final payout computation

However, there is no compensation provided for the distance travelled by the rider from their current location to the pickup point.
To improve rider fairness and acceptance for long-distance pickups, a new incentive component needs to be introduced.

Introduce a new incentive type:
Rider → Pickup location Distance Incentive (R2P Incentive)
This incentive will be calculated based on the estimated distance between:

Rider’s current GPS location (at time of order acceptance)
Pickup location

ERP Changes
Add a new incentive type:

RIDER_TO_PICKUP_DISTANCE_INCENTIVE
Configurable slab-based logic (same as existing P2D structure)

DE App Changes
Order Card / Order Detail/Order Notification:

Show earnings breakdown including:

Base Pay
Rider → Pickup Incentive (New)
Pickup → Drop Incentive
Other incentives (if any)
Total Estimated Earnings

Today’s Earnings: Include R2P incentive in total earnings calculation.

issues.author: Mokileswaran P
issues.subject: Intermediate Payout
issues.description:
To Test E2E Based on DE Intermediate payout -
1. Should be able to do day wise payout for the driver.
2.Weekly payout should not be any dependencies to affect this intermediate payout.
3.Should have seperate scheduler , once we run this intermediate batch should run based on the payout configuration.
4.If we configured to run only particular region then batch should create only for those region based on the DE DDT and if the batch split should be applied that also should be configured for example, if 1 region 2 DE is eligible for the 2 days payout, if we give 1 in the Config then 2 batch for the region with single DE it should create , if we give 2 then in single batch for the region both DE should be in that 1 batch for the payout.

Configurations - Refer to the attached image

customFields.name: Steps
customFields.value:
Configure DE intermediate payout for daily processing.
Select eligible DEs for the day (based on DDT).
Run the “Intermediate Payout” batch scheduler.
Ensure weekly payout is also enabled in the system.
Run the intermediate payout scheduler.
Check if weekly payout status or records impacted today's intermediate payout.
Configure a separate scheduler for intermediate payout.
Run only the intermediate payout scheduler manually.
Monitor logs and batch creation.
Configure payout to run for specific region(s) only.
Ensure DEs in that region have valid DDT records.
Run intermediate payout scheduler.
Batch Split Functionality Based on Config-
Region A has 2 eligible DEs for 2 days payout.
Set batch split config = 1 or 2.
Run intermediate payout scheduler.
Eligibility Check Based on DDT-
Update DDT so that only specific DEs qualify for payout.
Run intermediate payout scheduler.

E2E V-
Steps
Configure Region → DE → DDT → Payout Split.
Run scheduler.
Verify generated batches.
VeriFy payout values and DE count.
Validate no dependency with weekly payout.

customFields.name: Expected Result
customFields.value:
1.System should create daily payout entries for each eligible DE without errors.
2.Intermediate payout works independently.
3.Weekly payout configuration/status should not block or modify the intermediate payout.
4.Only Intermediate payout batch should run.
5.It should follow the payout configuration (region, splitting rules).
6.Batch should be created only for the configured region.
7.No batches should be created for other regions.
8.Batch count and DE distribution should match the configuration.
9.Only DEs that satisfy the DDT conditions should appear in the batch.
E2E-
Expected Result-
Batch created correctly.
DEs grouped correctly.
Amount calculated correctly.
Independent of weekly payout.

issues.subject: Restrict Vehicle Assignment to Single Active FTL Trip
issues.description:
In the FTL Fleet Trip module, a vehicle number should not be allowed in more than one active trip at the same time. A vehicle can be reassigned to a new trip only if the previous trip has reached the "Trip Ended/POD Pending" status.

If the vehicle is already assigned to an active trip
* Block assignment and show a warning:
  * “This vehicle is already assigned to another active trip.”

If the previous trip for the same vehicle is in “Trip Ended – POD Pending” status →
* Allow the vehicle to be assigned to a new trip.

If previous trip is in any other incomplete status →
* Restrict assignment.

issues.author: Sarat Chandran S
issues.subject: Vendor change request process
issues.description:
Similar to customer change request approval process flow to update in customer master there will be a vendor change request process flow for any change to be made tin the vendor data.

Attached process flow SRS document for reference. The attached srs defines the process flow of change in TDS deduction to be made in the vendor profile which needs to be done using vendor change request process
*4.1	Create Change Request*
User can update the TDS exemption using change request process inside vendor lead management. To raise a new change request user will login to Odoo and click on vendor lead management followed by clicking on “change request” option from the vendor leads main menu.
 
On clicking the change request option user will be directed towards change request creation listing view in which user will be able to create a new change request for the specific vendor.
 

User will then click on “new” button provided on the top left corner of the change request listing screen and system will direct the user towards change request creation form view as shown below in which they will enter the following requested details:
•	Customer name (drop down selection)
•	Vendor type (auto populated)
•	Phone number (auto populated)
•	Region (auto populated)
•	Service type (auto populated)
•	Fields to change (multi select)
  
Once the required fields have been selected user will select the TDS exemption or Low TDS exemption as the case may be and will click on “proceed” button on the top left corner of the change request form view.
Further to which system will display the current status of the selected field and user can change the TDS exemption option from “no” to “yes” or LOW TDS from “no” to “yes” and upload the exemption certificate to submit for unit head approval.
 
4.2	Change Request UH Approval
On submission UH will be notified by an email. UH can either click on the link provided on the email to directly view the change request submitted or can login to Odoo vendor lead management and select the change request under the status “Under UH approval” 
 
UH user can approve, reject or return the change request submitted. If returned then the change request will go back to the user who has created the CR for making necessary corrections. If rejected then the entire change request will not be editable for any further correction and user has to create a new CR and submit for approval.
When approved the CR goes to the next approval which is from the finance user.

4.3	Change Request Finance Approval
Finance user will be notified by an email when a CR is approved by UH. Finance user can either click on the link provided on the email to directly view the change request submitted or can login to Odoo vendor lead management and select the change request under the status “Under finance approval”
 
Finance user can approve, reject or return the change request submitted. If returned then the change request will go back to UH for making necessary corrections. If rejected then the entire change request will not be editable for any further correction and user has to create a new CR and submit for approval.
When approved the changes are automatically updated to the vendor profile in the vendor master.

issues.author: Mohammed Sadique
issues.subject: Display Updated Trip Margin Percentage Based on Final Vendor & Customer Charges
issues.description:
Currently, the trip margin is calculated based on the estimated vendor and customer charges stored in the Work Order. However, these values change later when additional charges are added and when final vendor bill and customer invoice amounts are generated.
The margin should therefore reflect the actual final bill and invoice values, not the initially estimated charges.

Update the margin calculation as follows:
* Vendor Final Amount: Use the final vendor bill total (including all extra vendor charges).
* Customer Final Amount: Use the final customer invoice total (including all extra billable charges).
* Margin Amount: Customer Final Amount - Vendor Final Amount
* Margin Percentage: (Margin Amount / Customer Final Amount) * 100

Display the updated Margin Amount and Margin % in the Work Order / Trip screen and ensure it auto-updates whenever:
* Vendor bill amount changes
* Customer invoice amount changes
No workflow logic changes are required — only recalculation and updated display.

issues.author: Sarat Chandran S
issues.subject: Fleet-FTL Trip Document verification stage
issues.description:
FTL TRIPS
1.	Create Trip
To create a new trip ops user log into Fleet management module and will select daily trips from FTL main menu:
 
Once the needed information has been entered the ops user will send the trip to next level of approval which will be “Document Verification Pending” stage. 
 

2.	Document verification Stage
After the trip is been created and user will click on send for approval button and the trip will then be sent to the next stage which is “document verification” stage.
At this stage the ops user/DMT personal will verify the trip documents before it is sent for ops manager approval.
The ops user will validate the document attached in the specific FTL trip and will either approve, return or reject the trip entered.
If returned the trip will be sent back to ops executive to make necessary changes and status of the trip will move to “new”.
If approved the trip will move from “document verification pending” to “pending approval” as per the current flow”
After the document has been verified the ops user will click on “verify” button on the top left corner of the trip form view as shown below and trip will move to ops manager approval.
 
3.	MU Approval
MU will be notified by email for the trip been sent for his/her approval. The mu can either click on link provided on the email or can login to Odoo fleet management module and can select the trip under status “pending approval” as shown below:
  
 
MU validates the details and will either approve, return or reject the trip. 
If returned the trip will be sent back to ops executive to make necessary changes and status of the trip will move from “pending approval” to “document verification pending”.
If approved the trip the status of the trip will move from “pending approval” to “manager approved”.
4.	Ops Manager Approval
Ops manager will be notified by email for the trip been sent for his/her approval. The ops manager can either click on link provided on the email or can login to Odoo fleet management module and can select the trip under status “manager approved” as shown below:

 
 
Ops manager validates the details and will either approve, return or reject the trip. 
If returned the trip will be sent back to ops executive to make necessary changes and status of the trip will move from “manager approved” to “pending approval”.
If approved the trip the status of the trip will move from “manager approved” to “Ops approved”.


5.	Finance Approval
Similar to ops manager finance manager will be notified by email for the trip been sent for his/her approval. The finance manager can either click on link provided on the email or can login to Odoo fleet management module and can select the trip under status “ops approved” as shown below:
 
 
Finance manager validates the details and will either approve, return or reject the trip. 
If returned the trip will be sent back to ops executive to make necessary changes and status of the trip will move from “under approval” to “manager approved”.
If approved the trip the status of the trip will move from “Ops approved” to “finance approved”.
6.	Send For Additional Charges Approval
6.1 Additional charges ops manager approval
If there is additional vendor charges entered such additional charges will have to be approved by Ops manager. Once the operations executive enters the additional charges to the trip he/she will click on “send for ops manager approval” and the additional charges will then be sent to ops manager approval.
If the ops manager rejects the additional charges, then the trip will be again sent back to ops executive for further correction.
Once approved the additional charge will then be sent to final approval which is done from the finance user.

 
 

6.2 Additional Charge Finance Approval
After the ops manager has approved the additional charges, the additional charges are then sent to finance approval. The additional charges will be validated and will be approved or returned as required. If returned the trip will move back to “Ops Approved” state.
To approve additional charges finance user will validate trip details and will click on “additional charges approve” button on the top left corner of the trip creation form view as shown below:
 
 
Please Note: Every time an additional charge is entered in the trip the ops user will have to sent it to approval from Ops manager and finance manager to finally add the charges to the trip.



7.	Trip Completion
To complete the trip ops user uploads the POD against the specific trip and ops user will click on “complete” button on the top left corner of the trip form view as shown below.
  

When ops user enters additional charges and submits for approval the trip moves to a new stage called “payment approval” which will be done by finance user. At this point the user will not be able to mark the trip as completed and will only be able to dot it once the trip has been payment approved by the finance user.
Once the additional information has been entered and sent to the finance user, finance user will be notified by an email notification or finance user can login to trip listing screen and he/she can filter “payment approval” trips and can approve or reject the trip.
If rejected the trip will go back to ops manager for correction.
On approval the status of the trip will move from “payment approval” to “payment approved”.

issues.author: Sarat Chandran S
issues.subject: Driver Management-Referral Bonus
issues.description:
The Referral Bonus Program is designed to incentivize existing delivery executives (DEs) to refer new drivers to the platform. This program encourages word-of-mouth recruitment and rewards both the referring DE. Referral bonus is structured as a weekly reward system.
Bonus Code & Naming Convention
•	Region – Region under where the Bonus will be available
•	Bonus Code: Code for the Bonus to show in the DE application
•	Bonus Name: E.g. Referral Bonus MAR 2024
•	Prefix for Referral Codes: Generated dynamically
Bonus Period & Eligibility Criteria
•	Start Date: Start date for the Bonus  
•	End Date: End date for the Bonus 
•	Maximum Redemptions per Referrer: No of time code can be used for a DE. 
•	Total Bonus Codes Issued: Total count of codes that have to be generated and assigned to DEs 
Referral Eligibility Criteria (Referring DE)
To be eligible to refer new DEs and receive the referral bonus, the existing DE must meet the following conditions:
1.	Joining Date – Date to be given in the application to calculate the seniority of the DE [ E.g. - must be after 01/10/2020]
2.	Total Attendance – Minimum number of Attendance required to refer. [e.g., must be 200 days or more.]
3.	Total Orders Completed – Minimum number of Orders DE should deliver to refer another DE [e.g., must be 1,000 or more.]
For the referring DE to receive the bonus, the referred DE must complete the required number of orders and attendance days as per the weekly or  monthly criteria.
Bonus Calculation
Weekly Bonus Structure for Referring DE
The referred DE must meet the following minimum order completion and attendance requirements:

Day range	Minimum Orders Required	Minimum Attendance (Days)	Bonus Amount (INR)
0-8	    20	5	100
8-15	25	9	200
16-21	30	12	300
22-28	40	20	500

Bonus Creation Module - In ERP 
DE App - Option for Eligible DE s to see the referral bonus. Option to use at the time of registration the referral code provided by co driver.

customFields.name: Steps
customFields.value:

"1. Navigate to Driver Bonus Payout Plan
2. Click +New
3. Fill Name, Region, Start/End Date, Category, Bonus Type, Applied On

"1. Navigate to 'Create Joining Bonus'
2. Leave out mandatory fields (e.g., Region or Start Date)
3. Click Save"
"1. Click +New
2. Leave Name, Region or Dates empty
3. Click Save"
"1. Open saved bonus plan
2. Click Add Driver
3. Filter and select DEs
4. Click Add"
"1. Open an existing plan with drivers
2. Click Remove Driver next to a DE
3. Confirm removal"
"1. Go to Weekly/Monthly Driver Payouts
2. Click +New
3. Enter From/To Dates, Region, Description
4. Click Recompute Lines
5. Validate payout details"
"1. Open payout record
2. Review values
3. Click 'Generate Payment Entry' and 'Generate Payable Entry' then check journal accounts"
"1. Create plan with customer restriction
2. Assign DE with matching and non-matching customer
3. Check eligibility"
"1. Simulate DE with less than required orders/attendance by end of plan
2. Check eligibility"
"1. Configure plan to track First Login Date
2. DE logs in
3. Bonus eligibility tracked from login date"
"1. Simulate DE completing all day ranges and associated orders/attendance
2. Check total bonus"
1. Simulate DE with 18 orders and 5 days attendance within 1-7 days range
"1. Assign DE to first bonus plan
2. Try assigning same DE to another plan with overlapping dates"
"1. Assign DE to plan
2. Simulate completion of 20 orders and 5 attendance days within 1-7 days range"
"1. Create plan for Live DEs
2. Assign Live and Dedicated DEs
3. Check bonus application"
"1. Enter Start Date > End Date during bonus creation
2. Click Save"
"1. Simulate attendance logs manipulation

"1. Assign DE to plan

When the default company of a user is changed from Tech to Fleet, the related partner's company is updated correctly to Fleet, but the associated employee's company remains unchanged. The Partner's company is updated to Fleet as expected.
The Employee's company remains as Tech instead of changing to Fleet.
Expected Result:
When the user's default company is changed to Fleet, both the Partner and the Employee should automatically update to Fleet to maintain consistency.
Suggested Resolution:
Update the logic to ensure that when a user's default company is modified, it triggers an update for both the Partner and the Employee records accordingly.

All fields in the list view should be read-only after the checkbox is selected.

issues.author: Mokileswaran P
issues.subject: Claim Flow
issues.description: Claim management module with happy flow and negative scenarios Test Cases.

customFields.name: Steps
customFields.value:
Happy Flow Test Cases:
1.Precondition: Claim Amount = Total Expense Amount
Steps:
Create a new claim
Add expense lines that sum exactly to the claim amount
Submit
2.Precondition: Total Expense > Claim Amount
Steps:
Add expense amount exceeding claim
Submit the claim
3.Precondition: Is Advance Needed = False
Steps:
Submit a claim without advance
Expense Manager approves
Claim gets approved and completed
4.Claim with Advance and Proper Approval
Steps:
Check “Is Advance Needed”
Provide advance amount
Expense Manager → Manager → Finance Approval
5.Cancelled Claim Flow
Steps:
User creates and submits a claim
Cancels before approval

Negative Flow Test Cases:
1.TC06 - Submit Without Expense Lines
Steps:
Create a claim
Do not add any expense line
Click Submit
2.Claim Amount Less than Advance Requested
Steps:
Claim Amount = ₹500
Advance = ₹600
3.Skip Expense Manager Approval When Required
Add high-value expense
Bypass Expense Manager role in workflow
4.Invalid Date Range in Expense
Steps:
Date From: 01-Apr-2025
Date To: 30-Mar-2025

Approval Flow Routing Scenarios:

Case	Condition	Flow
A	Total Expense ≤ Claim Amount	Submitted → Manager Approval → Done
B	Total Expense > Claim Amount	Submitted → Expense Manager Approval → Manager Approval → Finance Approval (if amount exceed from claim amount)
C	Advance Requested = Yes	Expense Manager → Finance Approval included
D	Claim cancelled	Status set to Cancelled
E	Claim approved but no advance taken	Status = Approved Without Advance

Approval Flow Routing Scenarios:
Scenario	Condition	Expected Routing Flow	Notes
S1. Normal Flow (No Advance)	Is Advance Needed = No
Total Expense ≤ Claim Amount	To Submit → Submitted → Manager Approval → Approved → Done	Simple claim without additional approval layers
S2. Advance Required Flow	Is Advance Needed = Yes
Advance Amount ≤ Claim Amount	To Submit → Submitted → Expense Manager Approval → Manager Approval → Finance Approval → Approved → Done (Before Expense line submission Advance should be with / without paid)
S3. Expense > Claim (No Advance)	Total Expense > Claim Amount
Is Advance Needed = No	To Submit → Submitted → Expense Manager Approval → Finance Manager Approval → Approved → Done Expense Manager must review (If Amount exceed)
S4. Expense > Claim (With Advance)	Total Expense > Claim Amount
Advance Needed = Yes	To Submit → Submitted → Expense Manager Approval → Manager Approval → Finance Approval → Approved → Done	Expense overage + advance = full flow
S5. Advance Paid = Advance Amount	Advance Paid = Advance Amount	... → Approved → Done	
S6. Cancelled by User	User Cancels after Submission	To Submit → Cancelled	Should not allow action once canceled
S7. Rejected by Any Role	Rejected by Manager / Expense Manager / Finance	To Submit → Rejected	Status locks in the Previous menu
S8. Approved Without Advance	Is Advance Needed = No
No Advance Paid	→ Approved Without Advance → Done

customFields.name: Expected Result
customFields.value:
1.Claim moves to Submitted → Manager Approval → Approved → Done
2.Claim goes to Pending Expense Manager Approval before reaching Manager Approval.
3.Status shows Approved Without Advance
4.Flow proceeds via each stage and finally reaches Done
5.Status = Cancelled

1.System shows validation error: "Please add at least one expense line."
2.Validation Error: "Advance cannot exceed Claim Amount."
3.System should block or auto-route to correct flow (no direct jump to Manager)
4.Validation error: "To Date cannot be earlier than From Date"

issues.author: Mokileswaran P
issues.subject: Test Case > Sales Module V16
issues.description:
# Verify clicking on "Sales module in v16" displays the dropdown menu with options like "Quotations," "Orders," "Sale Order Import," and "Customers" and "invoice" and "Products".
# Ensure the "Sales" menu is accessible on all relevant pages within the application.

customFields.name: Steps
customFields.value:
Sub-Menu: Quotations
1.Navigation
Verify that clicking on "Quotations" redirects to the quotations page.
Ensure that the URL changes accordingly (if applicable).

2.New Quotation Creation
Check if the "+ NEW" button opens a new quotation form.
Verify that all required fields (e.g., customer name, items, salesperson) are present in the new quotation form.
Test form validation by submitting the form with empty mandatory fields to ensure error messages are displayed.
Ensure that the quotation can be saved and appears in the list with a unique reference number.

3.Quotation Statuses
Verify that the different statuses (e.g., "Quotation Sent", "Cancelled") display correctly and update upon status change.
Check if users can change statuses according to permissions (e.g., only authorized users can cancel a quotation).

4.Quotation Search and Filters
Test the search functionality by entering valid and invalid query terms to confirm expected results.
Verify that the "Filters" button opens filtering options (e.g., date range, customer name).
Ensure that "Group By" and "Favorites" work as expected for easy access to saved searches and groupings.

Sub-Menu: Orders
1.Navigation
Verify that clicking on "Orders" redirects to the orders page.
Order List
Ensure that a list of orders displays, with columns like Order Number, Creation Date, Customer, Salesperson, Activities, and Status.
Confirm each column is sortable (if applicable) and provides correct order upon sorting.

2.Order Status and Confirmation
Verify that clicking "Set payments" under "Order Confirmation" brings up payment options.
Ensure that users can confirm or cancel an order with appropriate status changes.
Check if the payment confirmation updates the status from "Quotation" to "Sales Order".

Sub-Menu: Sale Order Import
1.Navigation
Verify that clicking on "Sale Order Import" brings up the import interface.
2.Import Functionality
Test importing a valid sale order file (e.g., CSV or Excel) and ensure data populates correctly with the Driver region should be same as the Customer region and Also based on the Excel Driver ID.
Check for error handling by uploading an invalid file format or corrupt data file.
Confirm that successful imports generate appropriate entries in the orders or quotations list.

3.Field Mapping
Ensure that the import tool allows mapping fields from the import file to the system’s order fields.
Verify that mandatory fields in the import file are flagged if missing during the import process.

Sub-Menu: Customers
1.Navigation
Verify that clicking on "Customers" navigates to the customers page.

2.Customer List
Ensure that the customer list displays relevant columns (e.g., Name, Contact Information, Orders Count).
Test if users can search, filter, and sort customers based on various criteria (e.g., name, email, or order count).

3.Customer Details
Check that clicking on a customer’s name opens their profile, displaying details like order history, contact information, and notes.
Verify that the customer profile allows editing, saving, and deleting (with confirmation if necessary).

4.Add New Customer
Test the "New Customer" functionality by verifying the form with mandatory fields, validation, and successful saving of customer data.

Sale Order Import -

1.Download Template
Verify that clicking "DOWNLOAD TEMPLATE" downloads the correct template file.
Ensure that the template file format is compatible with the system (e.g., CSV, XLSX).
Check if the template includes all necessary columns for importing a sale order.
Test if downloading is restricted to authorized users only.

2.Import
Verify that clicking "IMPORT" starts the import process using the uploaded file.
Check that the system shows a progress indicator or message during import.
Ensure that the import handles invalid data gracefully (e.g., displaying error messages for malformed rows).
Test if the system prevents import without selecting a file.

3.Upload Your File
Verify that clicking "UPLOAD YOUR FILE" opens a file upload dialog.
Ensure that only allowed file types (e.g., .csv, .xlsx) can be uploaded.
Check if large files display an appropriate loading indicator or progress bar.
Test for error messages if an invalid file format is uploaded.

4.Action
Verify that clicking "Action" displays additional actions available (e.g., duplicate, archive).
Ensure each action in the dropdown works as expected, such as duplicating or archiving records.

5.New
Verify that clicking "+ New" allows creating a new sale order import.
Check if unsaved changes prompt a warning before starting a new import.

6.Tabs
Draft Tab
Verify that the "Draft" tab shows all sale order imports with a draft status.
Ensure that moving a record from draft to another status is possible and functions correctly.
Check if draft records display relevant details like customer, item category, and status.

7.In Progress Tab
Verify that the "In Progress" tab displays all sale orders currently being processed.
Ensure that completed or draft orders do not appear in this tab.
Test that each record's status updates correctly when processing completes or fails.

8.Completed with Failures Tab
Verify that the "Completed with Failures" tab shows all sale orders that encountered issues.
Ensure error details are accessible for each failed import.
Check if records with minor issues (e.g., individual row errors) show partial success where applicable.

9.Completed Tab
Verify that the "Completed" tab lists all fully successful sale order imports.
Ensure that any completed orders display relevant details like order number and customer.
Test if completed records are locked from further edits or imports.

Form Fields
Upload File
Verify that the "Upload File" button opens a file selection dialog for uploading a sale order file.
Ensure that only files with supported formats (e.g., .csv, .xlsx) are accepted.
Check if an error message appears when trying to upload an unsupported file format.

Description
Verify that the "Description" field allows entering a description for the import.
Ensure that long descriptions are saved and displayed without truncation.

Customer
Verify that selecting a customer populates related fields if required (e.g., contact information).
Check that only valid customer names are allowed.
Test if a mandatory customer field shows an error if left blank.
Verify based on the customer selection all other fields such as Customer Industry, Item Category, Region, and Order Sales Person these are updated automatically after selecting customers from the dropdown or via search more in the dropdown.

Verify that the "Status" column shows the current status of each import (e.g., draft, completed).
Ensure that status updates correctly based on actions like import completion or failure.

customFields.name: Expected Result
customFields.value:
Clicking this button should send the quotation to the specified customer via email. Confirmation of email sent status should be displayed on the screen, and a record of the email should appear in the customer's communication history.
Clicking this button should convert the quotation into a sale order. The system should redirect to the sale order page, and the quotation status should update to "Sale Order Created" or similar.
Clicking this button should confirm the quotation as an official sale order. The system should lock fields to prevent further edits and display a confirmation message.
The "Order Lines" tab should display items or services added to the quotation, with options to add, edit, or delete line items. Totals should update dynamically.
Check The region field should reflect the customer’s region.

Sale Order Import Page - 
Download Template
Clicking this button should download a pre-defined template file in the correct format (e.g., .csv, .xlsx), including necessary columns for import.
The system should attempt to import data from the uploaded file. On success, it should display a success message and details of imported orders. If there are errors, a clear error message should display.
Clicking this button should open a file dialog to select a file for upload. Only supported file types (e.g., .csv, .xlsx) should be accepted, and invalid formats should trigger an error message.
Clicking this button should open additional actions (e.g., duplicate, archive). Each action should work as intended without affecting unrelated records.
Clicking "+ New" should start a new sale order import session, resetting form fields if already filled.
Tabs
Draft Tab
Displays all draft orders. Users should be able to edit or delete draft orders. Only draft orders should appear here.

In Progress Tab
Shows orders currently being processed. Users should see a progress indicator or message until processing is complete.

Completed with Failures Tab
Lists orders with partial or complete failures. Error messages should appear, indicating reasons for the failures.

Completed Tab
Displays orders that were successfully imported without issues. Each entry should be locked to prevent further edits.

Upload File
Clicking "Upload File" should open a file selection dialog. Selected files should appear as attached, ready for import.

Each field should accept valid entries based on pre-defined options or user input, populating data fields based on selection. Any missing required field should trigger a prompt or error.

Displays the order ID or number for each entry. Orders should link to detailed views if available.

Status Column
Shows the current status of each order (e.g., draft, in progress, completed). Status should update automatically based on actions taken.

issues.author: Mokileswaran P
issues.subject: Expenses claim
issues.description: Verify that the Expense Claim form can be submitted correctly with proper validations and behavior.

customFields.name: Steps
customFields.value:
Step 1: Open Expense Claim Form
Action: #Navigate to the page where the expense claim form is located.
Step 2: Verify "Requested By" and "Contact Number" Fields
Action: #Ensure the "Requested By" field is pre-populated with the correct user name (e.g., Mokileswaran) and the "Contact Number" (9600461909) is displayed properly.
Step 3: Enter Claim Details
Action: #Select a valid "Claim Type" from the dropdown.
#Enter a non-zero value for "Claim Amount" (e.g., 5000).
#Provide a reason for the claim in the "Claim Reason" field.
Step 4: Check "Is Advance Needed" Checkbox
Action: #Click on the "Is Advance Needed?" checkbox if an advance is required.
Add Comments (Not Mandatory)
Action: #Enter text in the "User Comment" section.
Step 6: Submit the Claim
Action: #Click the "Submit" button. 
Step 7: Approval Flow
Action: #Once submitted, the form should transition through various statuses such as "Pending Approval," "MU Approved," "Approved," and "Completed."
Step 8: Verify Form Behavior for Zero Claim Amount
Action: #Leave the "Claim Amount" as 0.00 and attempt to submit.
Negative case - Verify Required Fields
Action: #Try submitting the form without selecting a "Claim Type" or entering a "Claim Reason."

customFields.name: Expected Result
customFields.value:
#All fields should be displayed correctly and should either accept appropriate inputs or provide clear validation errors.
#Approval statuses should update accurately, and form should not be allowed to submit with missing or incorrect information.

1.Expense Claim form should be visible with fields for "Requested By," "Contact Number," "Claim Type," "Claim Amount," "Claim Reason," and others like "Comments" sections, and checkboxes.
2."Requested By" and "Contact Number" should be correctly auto-filled and non-editable if intended.
3.Claim Type" should be selectable.
4.Claim Amount" should accept numeric values.
5.Claim Reason" should allow free-text entry.
6.Checkbox should be clickable and toggle between checked/unchecked states.
7.Textbox should accept any valid characters, and the text should be saved properly.
8.The form should validate that all required fields (such as Claim Type, Claim Amount, Claim Reason) are filled, and submit the form if no validation errors occur.
9.After each approval stage, the claim should move to the next stage, with updates visible under the appropriate status.
10.An error should appear, preventing submission if the claim amount is zero unless this is allowed by the system.
11.The system should display validation messages highlighting the missing required fields.

issues.description:
ERP – CRM 
Customer: The users can be onboarded through our existing ERP process in the below module: 
There should be an additional field named-FIFO flow* (This is the maximum number of orders a DE can hold at a time for a customer)
The Field should carry the below options with it: 
No – The default selection will be NO while onboarding. 
Yes – In a box, the user must fill in the order limit number. 
Note – (No) will be the default selection for all the existing and new customers, which will run with our existing order process. If the User selects (Yes), they must mention the number of orders to be set for the customer as limit per DE, which will be a mandatory field, FIFO is selected as Yes. 
After this selection, all other existing functionality processes remain the same.
